# dsh-pinpu · Spectrum Rail

> Takes over the transcript's **own turn rail** — the marks down the right edge of the
> conversatio

n — and makes them dance to whatever the machine is playing, while
> replacing DSH's built-in "newes

t turn is highlighted" state with Codex's behaviour:
> nothing highlighted by default, highlight onl

y under the pointer, click-to-jump
> unchanged.

That is not an illustration. `tools/verify/rail-preview.mjs` builds a real Chromium
page from **the

shipped rail's own stylesheet and class names**, extracted from the
installed `dsh-client-ui-chat` b

undle, then loads the **real `lib/client.js`** and
drives it (only `/api/dsh-pinpu/spectrum` is stub

bed). The differences in mark length
*are* the spectrum: low frequencies at the foot of the rail, ne
xt to the newest turn.
Hovering brightens exactly one mark (the third screenshot from the same run):
## Install

- **From this repository**: add the GitHub repository `sqslm/dsh-pinpu` from DSH's plugin
page, the

same way any other GitHub plugin is installed, or
- **Locally packaged**: `node tools/install-profil

e.mjs` (`pnpm pack`, then write the package
into the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`; `--uninstall`

undoes it, `--dry-run` prints the
plan).
- **Restart DSH once** after the first install: the host ha

lf (capture, routes) is loaded at
process start, the browser half with the page.
- **No dependencies

to install**: the native capture module ships with the plugin (see
THIRD-PARTY.md), but it needs a

**CPython 3.12** interpreter — DSH bundles
one and the plugin looks for it on its own.
- **Windows o

nly** for now (WASAPI loopback). On Linux this needs a different source
(`getUserMedia` monitor or P
ulseAudio `.monitor`), which is not implemented.

## What it changes

The rail's states are CSS-module classes (`mark`, `markActive`, `markPreview`,
`markBusy`, `markUnlo

aded` → build-hashed `xpvNua_*` names). The plugin reads **no**
class name:

1. **Discovery by geometry** — inside `[data-conversation-scroll]`, find a group of
sibling buttons

with one size, one shared right edge and a constant vertical step
(≈10px). That group is the rail.
2

. **Tagging** — the container gets `data-pinpu-rail`, each mark `data-pinpu-tick="i"`
counting from

the bottom mark (0) upwards.
3. **Overriding with one `!important` stylesheet** —
- every mark becom

es the same dim colour and the same length, which removes the
built-in highlight *without knowing wh

ich class expresses it*;
- `:hover` brightens the mark under the pointer to full length — and only t

y`, detected from the `::before` animation)
is left alone so its pulse survives.

Click-to-jump is untouched: only the `::before` pseudo-element is restyled, the hit
area is still th

e app's own button, and its click listener still fires (measured in
the preview: `clicks delivered t
o the app handler: ["7"]`).
Measured in one preview run:
| State | Last mark (the built-in highlight) | Hovered mark | An un-hovered mark |

| before | `rgb(249,250,251)`, `scaleX(1)` | — | dim |
| after, playing | `rgba(255,255,255,.2)`, `s
## Audio: the system output itself (NetEase Cloud Music and friends)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- It captures the **loopback of the default output device** — literally what you hear.
No virtual ca

ble, and no player-specific support.
- To pin one device (headphones plugged in, but capture the onb

oard card), pick it in
the settings card's device list; empty means "follow the default output".
- C

apture happens in the **host half**: it runs `vendor/loopback.py` with the Python
the harness ships,

and that helper uses the **vendored PyAudioWPatch** (≈290 KB, the
PortAudio build with loopback sup

port) to open a `[Loopback]` input and stream mono
float32 PCM on stdout. The host does the FFT and

band mapping; the browser half only
draws.
- Therefore: **no microphone permission, no user gesture*

*, and not one line of capture
code in the renderer.

Why not `getUserMedia`: it can only open *capture endpoints*. Measured on this machine,
the registry

has `立体声混音 (Realtek USB Audio)` but disabled (`DeviceState=0x10000001`
where every endpoint Chromiu

m lists is `0x1`), so `navigator.mediaDevices` never shows
it; more importantly Stereo Mix mirrors *

*one** render device, and this machine listens
on that headset — so even enabled it would not carry

what you hear. Loopback of
the default output is the only thing that works.
## Settings (Settings → 频谱律动)

The host owns the **signal**, the browser owns the **presentation**. Everything is
`.volatile()`, so
edits apply live (mounting the bundle still needs one restart).
| Field | Default | Side | Meaning |
[该节后续省略]
### Why auto-gain

Measured with the preview harness: without normalisation, 24 bands span only
`0.51..0.76`, which dra

ws as six distinct lengths out of 37 — a flat wall. With it, the
same signal spans `0.18..1.0` and e

leven lengths. The same harness showed Chromium's
default `-100..-30 dB` analyser window pegs normal

ly-mastered material, so the ceiling
is raised to `-25 dB`.
## Known limitations

- The take-over depends on the rail's **geometry** (a column of equally sized,
right-aligned, evenly

stepped buttons). If DSH changes that layout the plugin will
simply not recognise the rail — it wil

l not damage the page, and the settings card
reports zero marks.
- It captures the loopback of the d

evice you selected; following the default output is
automatic, pinning a device is not.
- The number

of bands is the number of turns (one per mark); `minScale`/`maxScale` only
change the length range.

- A mark the app is animating (the busy pulse) does not dance; it keeps its own pulse.
- Loopback c

apture needs a PortAudio build with loopback support (the Windows wheel of
`pyaudiowpatch` ships in
the package); other platforms need their own.
